h: Cathedrals, Cavern and a Ferry Cross the Mersey
p: Clayton Square is right in the middle of Liverpool's shopping streets, just off Church Street, so you're in the perfect spot to explore on foot.

Music fans will want to head down to Mathew Street, home of the Cavern Club, where the Beatles played hundreds of times in their early years. The club is still running, and the street is lined with Beatles-themed pubs and shops.

Liverpool has two magnificent cathedrals, connected by Hope Street. The Anglican Cathedral is a huge sandstone building with a tower you can climb for amazing views, while the Metropolitan Cathedral, with its distinctive crown-like top, is a striking modern building. Walking between them along Hope Street is a lovely way to see a bit more of the city.
History fans should look up the Western Approaches museum, an underground wartime headquarters where the Battle of the Atlantic was coordinated. It's a fascinating peek into the Second World War.
And don't forget the classic: the Mersey Ferry runs river explorer cruises from Pier Head, with commentary on the city's history and views of the famous waterfront.
Bold Street, near the shopping centre, is packed with independent cafés and restaurants serving food from all over the world, so feeding the family is easy.
If it rains, Liverpool Central station is right next door, so hopping across the city on Merseyrail is easy.
With all of this on the doorstep, a session at Flip Out fits neatly into a packed day in one of the UK's liveliest cities.
